newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex tumbles on chart weakness.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex tumbles on chart weakness.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures prices fell sharply at the opening bell on Tuesday, pushed lower in technical trading through key chart support levels.

At 1045 EDT, crude for July delivery was down 83 cents at $20.80 a barrel. July unleaded gasoline was down 2.10 cents at 62.80 cents a barrel, while July heating oil was off 2.18 cents at 55.30 cents.
The decline in the complex was attributed mostly to a long-awaited technical correction to the gains posted over the past several weeks.
At the same time, there was talk that the sweeping election of political moderate Mohammed Khatami to the presidency of Iran indicated a shift in sentiment toward Islamic rule by Iran's populace.
A moderation in the political relationship between Iran and Western nations, especially the United States, could have implications for the oil sector in many areas.
"There are some traders today saying some of the drop is from the Iranian elections," one commission house trader said.
"But that news has been out over the weekend. I think we're just allowing for the correction that people have been waiting for for the past couple of weeks," he said.

Slipping refinery profit margins in some Asian areas had negative implications for the unleaded gasoline market, which has already been seen as failing to produce a summer-demand rally or to lead the complex at its customary time in spring.

Poor refining margins at Shell's 350,000 bpd Pernis refinery in Rotterdam have cut production there by about 14 percent beginning on Monday, following similar cuts at Texaco and British Petroleum's Nerefco plant last week.
Technical support for July crude, now a memory at $21.46, $21.16, $21.00 and $20.80, was seen between $20.40 and $20.50.
